skip_reason: Not a sales call. Inbound claims/damage call on a completed move from roughly three weeks earlier — the customer's mother's refrigerator door handle bolts were lost by the crew and the mover reportedly told her to buy replacements on Amazon herself. The entire 9.6 minutes is damage-claim intake, service recovery, crew-quality feedback on the Fort Worth branch, and routing (Erik texted the claims form link and his branch number). There is no quote, no pricing, no booking, and no prospective move anywhere in the transcript, so the 85-point sales scorecard does not apply.
top_strength: Not scored (claims call). Worth noting anyway: Erik named the crew's Amazon-link workaround as unacceptable rather than defending it, pulled up the move and crew names himself, committed to buying and replacing the bolts plus sending someone out to reinstall the handles, and pre-warned the claims team that the file was already three weeks old so it would be treated as urgent.
coaching_note: Not scored against the sales rubric. Two operational flags for Amanda rather than rep coaching: (1) a Fort Worth crew told a 71-year-old customer to order her own replacement refrigerator hardware on Amazon instead of filing a damage claim on site — that is a claims-process compliance gap worth tracing back to the crew, and Erik should have said 'the team should have filed a claim on site' as a correction to log, not just a note in passing; (2) the customer gave detailed, unsolicited crew-quality feedback (green mover, questionable truck packing, living room left blocked) on a ~$4,000 move and compared it unfavorably to two prior Einstein moves. That feedback has no capture path in this call beyond Erik's memory. Also note Erik committed to personally shepherding the claim while explaining he sits in Fort Worth and the customer reached the Dallas line — a single-point-of-failure handoff worth confirming actually landed with the claims team.
phone_presence_notes: Strong empathy and validation language throughout — 'that's not acceptable,' 'I'm sorry that was your experience with us,' 'I appreciate you being so kind and patient about it all, I know it's not exactly a fun thing to be dealing with especially when it's your elderly mother' — and the customer responded with 'That's amazing, thank you' and 'I really appreciate all your help'; held back from a 5 only because he repeatedly addressed her by a wrong or shifting name (Krista/Christian/Christina) and let long stretches of her feedback pass with bare 'Yeah' fillers.
